fixRound: FIX ROUND 2026-08-22 (review round 1 on this task). A controller review re-probed and re-cropped every spot and found that ALL FOUR shipped tilts (2, 12, 13, 20) had been fitted between two DIFFERENT physical objects -- the same failure class task 3 hit, and it survived an explicit warning. Every one of the four has been re-derived from scratch here by cropping both frames, naming the object at each row in words, and only then measuring. WHY THE OLD FITS LOOKED EXCELLENT, because this governs how the record must be read: a row read at a fixed column slides monotonically with tilt, so sweeping an UNRELATED render line into agreement with an unrelated photograph row ALWAYS converges, and converges tightly -- the discarded residuals were 0.0002-0.0065. A small residual is not evidence of correctness; it is a property of the method. The only thing separating a derivation from a coincidence is that the two rows are the same physical object, established by LOOKING. OUTCOME: kings-court ships NO pitch key at all. tour/apartments/kings-court.json is now byte-identical to main. That is a legitimate result, not a failure to try harder.
method: Same procedure as serenity's task 3 (as corrected 2026-08-22): for each compare spot a horizontal landmark is named by eye in the photograph and in the pitch=0 render (docs/superpowers/harnesses/2026-08-22-b4e/renders-pitch0-kings-court/), the object at each candidate row is named IN WORDS from a crop of both frames, and only a pair confirmed to be the same physical object is measured with tools/pitch_fit.py --probe. Candidate degrees are rendered live in the browser (?apt=kings-court&measure=1&fov=legacy, vertical fov pinned at 72, __measure()) and the same column re-probed. The chosen tilt MINIMISES the landmark-row disagreement, must be an interior point of the swept range and materially better than the 0deg disagreement -- there is no fixed tolerance (CORRECTED rule, task-3-brief.md). bandRows (0.0039) is used for ONE thing only: whether a confirmation capture reproduces a sweep capture of the same state. NEW IN THIS FIX ROUND -- landmark tracking. A row is followed across the sweep by predicting, from the exact pinhole relation at the pinned 72deg vertical fov, where a fixed world feature at the level-render row must land under the extra tilt, and then taking the probe candidate nearest that prediction. Measured rows agreed with prediction to <=0.004 of frame height in every round of every sweep below, which is what makes the claim 'this is one line, tracked' checkable rather than asserted; a naive nearest-previous-row tracker silently hopped between two lines 0.10 apart on 2.webp when it was tried first. deg is the config pitch convention (positive = looking down).

THE HONEST READING OF THE 17.38: it was not an improvement, it was four cameras tilted to align unrelated objects, and about 0.2 of dE2000 is what that bought.
